description: The privileged control window: application commands, approved-link opening among them, and the three core commands its frontend actually calls — event listen and unlisten for every subscription and its teardown, and event emit for the broadcasts it makes (the Settings section to open, the shutdown acknowledgement, and the embedded stage's viewport hints during a presentation, which the alignment engine's off-glass leash depends on). Nothing else from `core:default` is granted (#267). The menu bar is built and owned by Rust (src/menu.rs), there is no tray, and window operations — closing, focusing, presenting — are Rust commands, so the menu, tray, image, path, resources, app, webview and window plugins are withheld — all but the window plugin's `start_dragging` and `internal_toggle_maximize`, which Tauri's own drag script invokes for the toolbar band and the sidebar's head on a Mac, where the titlebar is an overlay the page runs under (`windows/material.rs`). Both take an optional window label, so a script here could name another of the app's windows; the only caller is the drag script, for the window it runs in, and the most either can do is move or zoom a window; with `core:default` a script here could have replaced the application menu with one of its own. That includes the debug-build devtools shortcut, which Tauri injects as a `plugin:webview` invoke: in a dev build right-click › Inspect Element still opens them, and release builds compile the command out. The dialog plugin is deliberately NOT granted — file pickers run in Rust (src/dialogs.rs) so no filesystem path is ever chosen by, or passed through, JavaScript (H5, spec §50.7). `core:window:allow-set-fullscreen` is deliberately NOT granted either: presentation is borderless (windows/present.rs), and the renderer calling OS fullscreen directly is what put a white bar over the opening of every take — withholding the permission is what stops that path being reintroduced by accident. `opener:default` is deliberately NOT granted either: it lets the webview open ANY url, and the one place the app needs it is a model licence link. That goes through `open_model_licence`, which checks the url against the licence urls the speech-model catalogue itself declares — so the webview can open exactly those and nothing else. Rust's own `reveal_item_in_dir` calls need no capability: capabilities gate the JavaScript→plugin path, and those run in Rust.
